name: Underwear as Outerwear
summary: Designers of the 1980s and 1990s took the corset, the cone bra and the slip out of the wardrobe and put them on the street. The bodices were boned satin and wool, worn as tops, jackets and dresses.

philosophy.core_thesis: What was hidden is now the dress: a corset, a bra or a slip shown in the open gives the body a built, public form.
design_principles: Cut the corset from historical patterns, with 10 to 20 boned panels and a busk or a laced back.
Boil down the idea to one garment: a boned bodice that stands as a top, a jacket or a dress.
Use outer cloth for the underwear shape: satin, wool tweed, leather or cotton drill.
Cone the cup in satin and set it at the bust, with a metal-cone bra for an extreme version.
Pair the corset with a plain skirt, a tailored jacket or trousers, so that the contrast shows.
Show the garment fully: a visible busk, a visible lace and a visible strap.
Add a slip dress in silk satin, 2 to 3 mm of seam and a bias cut.
anti_patterns: A corset hidden under a plain dress
A plain cotton bra with no structure
A costume pastiche with no tailoring
A hem and a neck that cover the garment

silhouette.shape: A built hourglass worn as an outer garment: a hard bodice, a bare shoulder and a skirt or trousers below.
silhouette.line: A strong curve from the bust to the hip, with the garment edge in plain view.
silhouette.fit: Close and firm at the torso, with the bone and the lace in the open; the lower half is loose or tailored.
silhouette.proportion: Waist 55 to 65 cm; corset length 30 to 40 cm; cone cup 12 to 15 cm out from the body.
rules: Cut the corset to be seen: finish the bone channels and the lace as decoration.
Pair the boned top with a long skirt, wide trousers or a man's jacket.
Set the neckline straight or at the bust line, with no cover.
Use a cone cup only as a large, bold shape.
Add a long coat or a jacket over the corset for the street.

fabrics.rule: Build the shape in satin or wool with steel boning, and trim it with lace, tulle and leather.

methods: boned panels from a historical pattern
bias-cut slip dress in silk satin
tailored skirt or jacket to go with it
construction.closures: A steel busk at the front or a cord lace at the back; some pieces use a hidden zip.
construction.details: Visible boning channels, bare lace at the top, metal eyelets, straps, and a ribbon at the waist.

surface.pattern: Plain satin or wool; for the street, a stripe, a check or a tweed; for show, beads and embroidery.
surface.gloss: Wool tweed at 2–6 GU; satin at 35–65 GU.
surface.wear: The satin shows creases at the waist, and the bone shapes itself to the body after a few wears.

palette.strategy: Skin tone, black and white for the base, with a bold colour or a tweed for the outer layer.

processes: pattern taken from a historical corset
boning cut and set in channels
satin cut on the bias for the slip
tailoring of the jacket and skirt
hand finish of the lace and the bone
making.scale: Made in a couture workshop and in a small factory in small lots. Shown on the runway, then copied for the street and in the high street shop.
making.signs: Visible boning and lace, a corset cut worn as a top, an outer cloth on an inner shape, and a tailored piece to match.

pieces.form: Boned satin corset worn as a top over trousers
Boned bodice in wool tweed worn as a jacket
Satin cone bra worn as a top
Bias-cut silk slip dress worn for the street or for the evening
Stretch bodysuit worn as a top under a jacket

positive: boned corset worn as a top

canonical_works.work: Corset dress with a cone bra
Cone-bra corset of the Blond Ambition tour

evidence.title: Cone-bra corset of the Blond Ambition tour, 1990

emotion.target_response: A feeling of daring and control: a private garment in public, built with the craft of the tailor.

use_cases: a runway or editorial fashion brief
a museum label or exhibition study
a fashion image prompt for a corset look
avoid_when: the brief wants a soft or natural body line
the brief is a historical reconstruction of corsets under a gown

modifiers.how: Add straps, chains, ripped tartan and a harsh cut; keep the boned corset as the centre.
Add a sharp-shouldered jacket, a pencil skirt and a plain colour; keep the boned top.

ornament_level.note: A tailored corset is plain; a couture one carries beads, lace and embroidery.
